newsitem.title: USA: Burlington results helped by prices, volumes.
newsitem.headline: Burlington results helped by prices, volumes.

text.p: Burlington Resources said Thursday that third quarter 1996 results were "fueled by increased prices, volumes and expanded margins."

In a release Thursday the company said that gas volumes increased despite pipeline outages and plant maintenance in the San Juan Basin. It said that the increase in volume resulted from exploration and production success in the Gulf of Mexico.

Burlington President and Chief Executive Officer Bobby Shackouls said in the release that "this quarter was one of the strongest in the company's history and the fourth consecutive quarter of increased earnings."
"Natural gas prices in the west, particularly in the San Juan Basin, continue to increase," he said.

Realized natural gas prices in the third quarter 1996 increased to $1.94 per thousand cubic feet (mcf) from $1.16 per mcf for the same period in 1995, while third quarter realized oil prices moved up to $21.25 per barrel from $16.68 per barrel for the same time last year.
Burlington also said that it has made a strategic move to deeper water in the Gulf of Mexico and that exploration opportunity exists on its large onshore acreage base.
